outcomes: The CI log of a change names the components it changed and the components that depend on them, inferred from the repository's own manifests
The same log gives the tests and the line coverage of each component, and the coverage of the lines the change added or modified

The same log lists the packages whose locked version the change added, removed, upgraded or downgraded and, when the CI wrote a software bill of materials, the known vulnerabilities each one fixes and introduces and its licences before and after
The evidence document carries the same facts and validates against protocol/evidence v1
nonGoals: Reading a putnami.workspace.json through go.putnami.dev/cli/model: a Putnami workspace runs its own extensions
Running a package manager, an orchestrator or the tests
Querying a vulnerability database or running an SBOM tool: the CI writes the CycloneDX or SPDX document, observe reads it
Attributing a JUnit case by a class name that names no repository file, when neither its file nor its report lies in a component

requirements.text: The Nx, Node workspace, Composer, Go and Python detectors answer for the repository. When two name one directory, the higher source wins: orchestrator, then workspace, then manifest. A changed file belongs to the innermost component that holds it. A component is changed when one of its files changed, dependent when it reaches a changed one through its edges. Edges to an unknown component are dropped. When no detector finds a component, the repository is one fallback component.

A JUnit case goes to the component that holds its test file, named by its file or class name as a path or, for pytest, its dotted class name as a module, else to the component of the Go package its suite names, else to the one that holds its report. A covered file goes to the component that holds it. A report path is read as repository-relative, relative to the report's component or directory, absolute, or as a Go import path. Each component sums its cases, their duration and its lines.

The lines a change added or modified are the added lines of the diff from the merge base to the head, with no context. Each changed file that still exists and that a coverage report instruments gets its covered and instrumented changed lines and its uncovered line numbers. A line two reports instrument is covered when either covers it. Without a base or a coverage report, there is no changed-line coverage.

Each changed package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, composer.lock, go.mod, uv.lock and poetry.lock is read at the merge base and at the head. A package present on one side only is added or removed; one whose versions differ is upgraded, downgraded or, when they do not compare, changed. Workspace links, path, editable and directory packages and modules of the repository are no dependency. A Python package name is normalized. A lockfile that cannot be read is a diagnostic.

The text summary lists the changed and dependent components: a dependent one names the components it depends on, a changed one the other changed components it reaches, directly or not. It then lists each component's tests and coverage, the changed-line coverage with its least covered files, and the dependency changes. --output=json prints the same observation. --evidence writes the components with their impacts and edges and the same analyses, valid against protocol/evidence v1.

A software bill of materials (SBOM) is a CycloneDX 1.4 to 1.6 or SPDX 2.3 JSON document the CI wrote. The head one is the file --sbom names, else the one discovery finds by content among .json files whose name holds bom, cdx, cyclonedx or spdx; the base one is the file --base-sbom names, never discovered. Several head documents, a named file that is not one, or one that cannot be read is a diagnostic, and that side is unknown.

Each dependency change gets, per side whose SBOM lists the package at a version the lockfile locks there, its licences and known vulnerabilities, matched by ecosystem, name and version through the package URL, pypi to a Python lockfile. The summary gives per change the vulnerabilities it fixes and introduces, or the known ones at the head and an unknown base without a base SBOM, and the licences before and after. Without an SBOM, the summary and evidence are unchanged.
